title: RPG Maker Mz crashes when I open the database and try and import/create new tileset s.

posts.author: duk
posts.body: Every time I open the database on RPG maker mz to try to upload a new tileset, it takes a very long time to open the tilesets folder, and more often than not, will crash before I get a chance to upload/select my tilesets. There is no error message, the engine simply closes itself. This issue doesn't happen every time but often enough that it becomes very annoying and inconvenient. Is there a possible solution for this?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
that often happens if either the folderpath or the filenames break the HTML-rules for names.
what is the full folderpath (beginning with the drive letter) to the tilesheet images, and how did you name those files?

posts.author: duk
posts.body:
This is the path: C:\Users\jeff-\OneDrive\Desktop\0\wisewolf_games\Tsuki Harvester\img\tilesets
To be honest I am unaware of the HTML-rules for names. I download free/paid tilesets off itch.io and just export the files/folders to my tilesets folder.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Just to offer a contrary opinion...I don't see how the file names could have anything to do with it.
The editor is not coded in an HTML-based language, so there's no reason it would crash if your filenames weren't compatible with those rules. In fact, we see tons of people who have incorrect file names and don't know it's a problem until they deploy their game for other people to play.
Additionally, if you're saying that the editor is crashing before you start browsing for the files, then those file names aren't connected to anything in the editor at that point.
That doesn't mean you shouldn't be aware of HTML file name conventions (no spaces or special characters), but I can't see how it would apply here.
What operating system are you using? Have you uninstalled and reinstalled the software?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
One of the rules you already have broken is "no spaces" - there is a reason why on the internet the files use the underscore, and you have a space between tsuki and harvester.
Other rules are only latin letters, arabic numbers and very few special signs. Or that capitalisation counts even if windows ignores that.
Second problem is OneDrive. Only one application can open any one file at a time, and if OneDrive is making a sync that will block the editor from opening the files. You should place your working directory outside OneDrive

posts.author: Winshifter
posts.body:
I don't think is the folder path or the name, I have folder names of projects that break the html format and MZ editor works normally.
When MZ was released, I had the same issue, but with anything I used the browser part, even seleciting a project that was already created. I complained and even support didn't have any clue as to what the hell was going on. The solution that eventually worked was buying a new computer. In my case, I was already in the process of buying a new one, but because of other reasons (had a small accident and computer wasn't working properly, but was not the reason of the issue with MZ). This issue by the way only happened in MZ, on MV, VXAce or even XP this didn't happened, so because of the MV version the "breaks the HTML rules" might make the cause to not apply.

There are consequences to placing your working folder outside of OneDrive, so any such advice should be weighed against this.
